title: Joining Charlie Johnson in Atlantic City and the 'Paradise' name
summary: Waters headed for a big band via Philadelphia, joined Johnson in Atlantic City knowing New York was next, and claims the Paradise Ten name came from both the Atlantic City and Small's Paradise.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: But you went from Boston to Philadelphia, not Boston to New York. What was the line of reasoning?
To join a big band.
So you got a gig, you wanted to get out of Boston, you were hopin' to get a gig in New York, but as it turned out you got a gig -
Yeah, I'm on my way to New York, see. I'm going home because I live in Pennsylvania.
Uh huh.
But you're playing at -
I'm quitting all these pupils and everything that I have in Boston to go home.
But not to where, you said a second ago you quit Boston to go to New York, now you're saying you're quitting to go to Pennsylvania. Which was it?
Well that's where I said I made a mistake of the biggest, first big band that I worked, remember I told you I made a mistake -
Yeah, I remember, but even if it was Charlie Johnson it wouldn't have been New York, it would have been Atlantic City.
Oh no no. Charlie Johnson was established in Small's Paradise -
Benny Waters 50HP 6/6/82
When you joined it?
Sure, he was just workin' down there season, three months -
Oh, it was just 'cause it was the summer -
Sure -
so you knew you were gonna go to New York -
Sure, sure -
Oh, I get you -
that would be natural. I mean, I don't know how many years, three months in Atlantic City Paradise, the rest in Small's Paradise. Three months, we did that for years -
But they started it, the Paradise in Atlantic City, that's where the Paradise came from, it was a coincidence that they played Small's Paradise in New York.
No, no, 'cause Paradise came from New York. He was in New York and before he went to Atlantic City.
Uh huh. Well, a little while ago you said the Paradise came from the Paradise in -

Two Paradises, Paradise Atlantic City - I say that's where the name, he's got his name, Paradise Ten because he played in the Paradise in Atlantic City and the Paradise in New York, that's what I'm sayin'. That the way -
So you're saying it's both.
That's the way it got its name from.
But not the -
By bein' in two Paradises, it's easy to say Paradise Ten.
Were they the same ownership?
No, no. No, it had nothin' to do with Small's. Small's was Negro, see.
